title: Energy accounting and conditional conservation of mechanical energy

authority_basis.claim_scope: Current Grade 9 curriculum requires mechanical energy, PE-KE conversion in free fall, and the law of conservation of energy.

Technical Engineering distinguishes total energy conservation from conditional mechanical-energy conservation by making the chosen system, non-conservative transfer, dissipation, and model conditions explicit.

concepts.statement: Energy accounting begins by declaring the physical system; changing the system boundary can change whether an interaction is represented as external work or as a change in an internal energy store.
concepts.why_required: The same physical event can be represented consistently in different ways only when the system boundary is explicit.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Work terms and potential-energy changes can be double-counted, omitted, or silently moved across the boundary.

concepts.statement: Mechanical energy in the governed Grade 9 model is the sum of kinetic energy and the included potential-energy store, E_mech = K + U.
concepts.why_required: It defines the quantity whose constancy is often—but not always—available as a simplifying model.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Conservation language can be used without specifying which energy stores are being summed.

concepts.statement: Energy conservation requires accounting for energy transfers and store changes across the chosen system rather than assuming one selected form of energy remains constant.
concepts.why_required: It preserves conservation when mechanical energy changes because energy is transferred or transformed into other forms.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Frictional or other dissipative cases can be described as destroying energy or can be solved by invalidly holding K+U constant.

concepts.statement: K + U is constant between two states only when the chosen mechanical-energy model has no net non-conservative work or unaccounted dissipative transfer across the relevant interval.
concepts.why_required: The law of conservation of energy does not imply unconditional conservation of mechanical energy.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: A memorised K_i+U_i=K_f+U_f equation can be applied even when friction or another transfer changes mechanical energy.

conditions: K and U refer to the same chosen system and state
The same potential-energy convention is used across compared states

symbols.name: net work by included non-conservative external interactions in the chosen model

conditions: Potential-energy terms represent the conservative interactions included in the chosen system/model
Non-conservative work is defined consistently with the chosen system boundary
All terms refer to the same initial-to-final interval
W_nonconservative = 0 for the chosen mechanical-energy model over the interval
No relevant dissipative transfer is omitted
Initial and final states use the same potential-energy reference and motion frame

model_conditions.condition: The object/system boundary and the interactions represented inside versus across that boundary are declared before choosing the energy equation.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Boundary choice determines whether an interaction appears as external work or as a change in an included energy store.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Work and potential-energy terms can be double-counted or omitted while appearing algebraically plausible.

model_conditions.condition: Use K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f only when net non-conservative work is zero and no relevant dissipative energy transfer is omitted for the chosen interval.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Total energy conservation is broader than conservation of the selected mechanical-energy stores.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Mechanical energy is incorrectly kept constant in frictional or otherwise dissipative cases.

model_conditions.condition: When friction or another dissipative interaction is non-negligible, its energy transfer or resulting non-mechanical store change must be represented rather than silently discarded.
model_conditions.physical_reason: Dissipation changes mechanical energy without violating total energy conservation.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: The model can falsely report missing or destroyed energy.

representations.semantic_geometry: A boundary encloses the chosen object/system, labels included energy stores, and marks work or other energy transfers that cross the boundary over the interval.
must_not_imply: a boundary choice changes the physical prediction when the accounting is complete
representations.verification_method: Check that every retained energy store and every crossing transfer belongs to the declared system and that the same physical event gives compatible predictions under an alternative valid boundary choice.

representations.semantic_geometry: Initial and final bars show relative amounts of K and U, with an explicit transfer/dissipation channel when mechanical energy changes.
mandatory_elements: transfer or dissipation channel when required
forbidden_omissions: transfer/dissipation when K+U is not constant
must_not_imply: bar height is an empirically calibrated learner measure
K+U must have equal initial/final totals when non-conservative work is present
representations.verification_method: Translate the bars back to the symbolic energy relation and verify the same change/transfer balance and limiting cases.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Choose and state the physical system and the initial/final states before writing any conservation equation.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The same interaction can be represented simultaneously as external work and potential energy or omitted entirely.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Inventory the relevant K/U stores and identify energy transfers, including non-conservative or dissipative interactions, across the chosen interval.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: Mechanical energy can be assumed constant before checking whether a transfer changes it.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Use the mechanical-energy change relation when non-conservative transfer is present; simplify to K_i+U_i=K_f+U_f only when its conservation condition is established.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The law of conservation of energy is reduced to an unconditional mechanical-energy equation.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Solve the state relation and verify units, common references, sign of transfers, limiting cases, and consistency with the declared boundary.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: A numerically plausible result can retain a hidden reference, sign, or dissipation error.

required_transformations.description: Translate the scenario into an explicit system boundary, initial/final states, energy stores, and crossing transfers.
Select the general mechanical-energy change relation and simplify to mechanical-energy conservation only when non-conservative transfer closes to zero.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: Because energy is conserved, K + U must be constant in every mechanical situation.
misconceptions.why_plausible: The broad conservation law is often remembered as one convenient mechanical-energy equation without its applicability conditions.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A sliding object slowed by kinetic friction loses mechanical energy while the broader energy account includes energy transferred to non-mechanical stores.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Use a system-boundary energy diagram or energy-state bars with an explicit dissipative transfer channel.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Use Delta(K+U)=W_nonconservative or an expanded energy account; set W_nonconservative to zero only when justified.
misconceptions.verification: Compare otherwise identical frictionless and frictional cases; only the frictionless mechanical-energy model should retain constant K+U.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: A decrease in mechanical energy due to friction means energy has been destroyed.
misconceptions.why_plausible: Only K and U are tracked while thermal/internal or environmental transfers are omitted from the representation.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: The decrease in K+U can be matched by energy transferred to other stores while total energy remains conserved.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Expand the energy account beyond K and U or mark the transfer crossing the chosen boundary.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Distinguish conservation of total energy from conservation of the selected mechanical-energy stores.
misconceptions.verification: Check that the expanded account balances even when mechanical energy decreases.

problem_families.name: Potential-to-kinetic energy conversion in free fall
problem_families.first_technical_move: Declare the object-Earth energy model and verify negligible non-conservative transfer before equating initial and final mechanical energy.
fatal_errors: assuming K+U constant with non-negligible resistance

problem_families.name: Mechanical-energy change with friction or other non-conservative work
problem_families.first_technical_move: Declare the system and determine whether frictional/non-conservative interaction is internal to the expanded energy account or appears as work/transfer across its boundary.
fatal_errors: setting K_i+U_i=K_f+U_f despite nonzero non-conservative work
double-counting frictional work and the same internal-energy increase

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Remove the conditional-conservation invariant so K+U can be treated as constant in frictional cases.
Remove the explicit system-boundary requirement from the conservation model.
